faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for an Emirates cabin crew member under the award?
faqs.a: Under the Aircraft Cabin Crew Award 2020, the minimum hourly rate for a cabin crew member is $28.88 per hour as of 1 July 2026. This applies to full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $36.10 per hour. Emirates may pay above these minimums, but the award provides the legal floor.

faqs.q: How is casual loading calculated for cabin crew, and does super apply on top?
faqs.a: Casual loading is 25% of the base hourly rate, paid instead of leave and other entitlements. For a cabin crew member on $28.88, the casual rate is $36.10. Superannuation is paid on top of the ordinary earnings at 12% (from 2026–27), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So the total cost to the employer includes the hourly rate plus super.

faqs.q: What is the annual salary for a full-time cabin crew member based on the award rate?
faqs.a: Using the formula hourly rate × hours per week × 52, a full-time cabin crew member at $28.88 per hour working 38 hours per week earns approximately $57,070 per year. bodyMarkdown:
## Emirates Cabin Crew Salary: Understanding the Award Rates

When researching the **emirates cabin crew salary**, it’s important to start with the legal minimums set by the Fair Work Commission. The Aircraft Cabin Crew Award 2020 [MA000047] covers cabin crew members, supervisors, and managers working on regional, domestic, and international flights. While Emirates may offer salaries above the award, the award provides the baseline for pay calculations in Australia.

### Minimum Rates Under the Award

According to the page, the minimum weekly rate for a full-time cabin crew member is $1,097.40, which equates to $28.88 per hour. For a cabin crew supervisor on narrow-bodied aircraft with four or more crew, the rate is $1,280.40 per week ($33.69 per hour). A cabin crew manager on wide-bodied aircraft earns $1,495.50 per week ($39.36 per hour). These rates apply from 1 July 2026 and are updated annually.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual cabin crew members receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a cabin crew member, that means $36.10 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. Superannuation is paid on top of ordinary earnings at the legislated rate of 12% (from 2026–27), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if you’re a casual cabin crew member earning $36.10 per hour, your employer also contributes $4.33 per hour to your super fund.

## How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

To estimate your annual gross pay, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full-time employee, the standard assumption is 38 hours per week. For example:

- Cabin crew member: $28.88 × 38 × 52 = $57,070 per year
- With super at 12%: $57,070 × 1.12 = $63,918 total package

If you’re casual, use the casual rate: $36.10 × 38 × 52 = $71,334 per year, plus super of $8,560, totalling $79,894.

### Fortnightly Pay

A fortnightly gross pay is simply the weekly amount multiplied by two. For a full-time cabin crew member at $28.88 per hour, weekly pay is $1,097.40, so fortnightly is $2,194.80. This is useful for budgeting if you’re paid every two weeks.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates from the [Australian Taxation Office](/topics/take-home), the first $18,200 is tax-free. Then:
- $18,201 to $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 to $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 to $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a full-time cabin crew member earning $57,070, the estimated tax is about $8,716 plus $1,141 Medicare, leaving a take-home of around $47,213 per year. This is before any salary packaging or deductions.

## Comparing to the National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. The cabin crew award rate of $28.88 is about 9% higher. Casual loading brings it to $36.10, which is 37% above the minimum. This reflects the specialised nature of cabin crew work.

## Conclusion

While the exact **emirates cabin crew salary** may vary based on experience, allowances, and enterprise agreements, the Aircraft Cabin Crew Award provides a clear starting point. Understanding the minimum hourly rate, casual loading, and super ensures you can compare offers and negotiate effectively. Remember that annual pay is an estimate based on consistent hours and no overtime. For personalised calculations, always refer to your employment contract and the Fair Work Ombudsman resources.
